subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Tactics in Net/Wall, Striking/Fielding, and Target Activities
essentialQuestion: How do you make an opponent or a target problem easier before you solve it?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of creating and exploiting space across a net in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe shot selection and risk management using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply striking and fielding placement, positioning, and anticipation in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving target activities: routine, consistency, and pressure management; correct it and explain why.
Connect scoring systems and how they change optimal strategy with self-scouting: knowing your own tendencies and explain how one affects the other.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build a tactical profile for one activity — strengths, tendencies, and the two adjustments most likely to improve results — then test it and revise.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Court size, target distance, implement, and object speed are learner-set. Seated, one-handed, and reduced-range versions are provided for every activity.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
